quest.title: For a Green Island...
quest.description: You discover an island affected by kuuvahki turbulence near Hiisi Island...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *cough cough* We finally made it out... Ugh, Paimon didn't expect that collapse... That was so scary! Good thing we managed to find another exit...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But with all that noise just now, Verna must have heard it too, right? Paimon had better hurry back and bring her here before she tries to dig into the cave. She might get herself trapped...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Taking advantage of her ability to fly, Paimon goes around the other side of the mountain and brings Verna over, all while explaining to her everything that just happened...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #Huh? It c—collapsed!? Oh no, how did this happen... {NICKNAME} and Paimon, are you both alright!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean you didn't hear that huge noise just now?! And it's a little late to say "are you alright," isn't it? We're standing here, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Haha, sorry... I was busy calibrating Kraka III, so I wasn't paying attention...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #Indeed, you have proven exceptionally trustworthy, {NICKNAME} — more so than even myself as a priestess. Had I encountered such circumstances, I fear I would have been at a complete loss.

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #Alright, let's see what you've been up to, little Krakas... Well, aren't you a right troublemaker! You found the pieces, but didn't come back on time, so {NICKNAME} and Paimon had to turn this place upside down just looking for you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, they found the pieces, but got stuck on their way back... Don't you think you might've messed the settings up somewhere, Verna?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Certainly not! I'm a direct apprentice of the famous "Papa Wrench," and the finest mechanic on Hiisi Island! There's no way I'd mess up a simple recall function... Nope! Definitely not!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't think Paimon didn't hear you hesitate! And let's face it — bad recall function or not, they didn't return, and that's a fact!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Oh, but they have returned. You two reliable souls did bring them back, didn't you? Now all we have to do is toss this fragment up like you did previously, and everything should go off without a hitch!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're seriously sidestepping the issue here...

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: As the sacred prayer goes: "O, great father of genesis, forger of the{RUBY#[S]Takoja Ianikuinen} tripled moons! Let your wrath right that askew throne, that the fair one may become thy..."

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Become thy... uh, what comes next?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Argh, forget the chant! Scientifically speaking, no matter the problem, a few good whacks will do the trick! Percussive maintenance, go!

choices.text: Yeah, science!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Whether it's Treasure Hoarders, Specters, or troublemakers from who knows where — just whack 'em a few times and you're good to go...  Wait, how's any of this even remotely "scientific"?!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No matter how Paimon looks at it, something about this plan feels off... Are we sure we won't accidentally blow the whole island sky high?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Haha, you're a funny one, Paimon! Nobody would be silly enough to blow their own home apart, right?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Rest assured! I've been secretly... ahem, I mean, I've been thoroughly researching this for a long time, and can vouch that it is a very reliable plan! And we did test it once just now, didn't we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Guess we've got no choice but to try at this point...

choices.text: Riiight... Are we sure this won't go horribly wrong...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... You can't phrase this in a way that doesn't sound risky!

talks.objective: Investigate Thunderclap Reef

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's that over there...?

talks.objective: Follow the robot
Investigate Thunderclap Reef

dialogues.text: Huh? Kraka III, you're back already?
That's weird. You didn't collect the fragment, so why are you here so soon...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Hello?
Ah! I'm sorry, I'm sorry! Please let me explain! There's a really good reason I'm dressed like this — it's not heresy or anything, I swear!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wah! Paimon hasn't even said anything yet!

Huh? Oh, you're just an adventurer from the outside... By the Moon Goddess's silken locks, I thought you were— Wait a sec! Why are you dressed like that? And acting like it's totally normal, to boot!?

choices.text: Well, it's my favorite outfit.

response.text: Wait... You must be... You're the one the Moon Ma{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}iden holds dear... Talented beyond belief and totally unfazed, even with all this <color=#00E1FFFF>kuuvahki turbulence</color>...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, about that... Well, Paimon thinks we can just skip over the details. But seriously, why are you dressed like that? What are you doing here? And what even is kuuvahki turbulence?

Ah, pardon my rudeness. Ahem! "I am she who serveth the Frost Moon, born of the tides, and bearer of the High Priestess's mantle beneath the moon's silver gaze. In this sublunary sphere, I am known as Vernadska."

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: But you two can just call me Verna. I'm currently on a very secret mission to restore balance to the kuuvahki here. So, if I may — how should I address you both?

choices.text: #In this sublunary sphere, I am known as {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Copying the way she talks? Really? Fine, fine — ahem! In this sublunary sphere, Paimon is... Paimon! Ugh... That was super embarrassing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And wait, you mentioned you're on a secret mission... It's not very secret if you just tell us immediately, is it? And calling yourself a "High Priestess" while dressed like that? You ain't fooling anyone, Miss...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Well! You can't judge a book by the cover it wears, yes? We, too, have had scammers parading around Nasha Town in Frostmoon robes they clearly "found" somewhere.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Oh! I know! A demonstration of our ancestors' bles{RUBY#[D]kuuvahki}sings should convince you of my identity! Bear witness... Hi-yah!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh, {NICKNAME}? Seems to Paimon like we bore witness to a whole lot of nothing...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: ...Oops. I forgot this outfit wards off kuuvahki. Hang on, I'll take it off and try again...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Oh, but with the turbulence afoot, I might get a little nosebleed without my suit... Well, since it won't take long, I guess I'll be fine!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Okay, first I'll undo this strap here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, wait, wait! No need to go that far! We believe you, just keep the suit on!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Great! Does that mean you two would be willing to help me with my mission?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh, {NICKNAME}, did Paimon pass out for a minute or ten? Why's she suddenly asking us about some promise we've never heard about? She's gotta be a fake, Paimon's sure of it...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: I told you, I'm not faking... Ugh, forget it. Let's put my identity aside for now. Like they say, small slips sink big ships.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: If we leave the kuuvahki turbulence alone, we'll have a catastrophe on our hands before long!

choices.text: Then you should get more people to help.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Unfortunately, I can't. The others don't have my level of resistance. If I call in backup, they'll be dealing with much, much worse than a simple nosebleed.  That's why having helpers like you two show up is a rare stroke of luck!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, fine! We're adventurers, and we don't say no to folks in need, even if you seem a bit... unreliable. But even Paimon can tell something's definitely off here. Maybe we can help!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Excuse me? I'll have you know I'm the most reliable priestess there is! And you two seem even more reliable, so I'll share this super-duper reliable, foolproof plan with you!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Let's cut to the chase — those two rotating boulders are the cause of this kuuvahki turbulence.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Ever since the time of the <color=#00E1FFFF>first Moonchanter</color>, Lady Aila, the kuuvahki in Thunderclap Reef has always been unstable. But things have gotten worse since those two large rocks fell from the sky...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: As the scripture says: "O Moon Ma{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}iden, even the immutable laws set by the dread Sovereign of the Firmament shall bend to your song, and even the tides of time and heaven's signs will..."

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Will... Uhh... what was the next line again? Oh well, I'm sure you get the idea!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets the idea... that you're super unreliable!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Oh, come on, forgetting one little verse in a prayer doesn't make me a bad priestess! Besides, we're not counting on prayers to fix this — we're using science!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Based on my calculations, those two stones are filled with powerful kuuvahki energies, which is why the balance here is particularly messed up.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: The solution's simple. We're going to fight fire with fire! If we use other kuuvahki-charged fragments and hit those boulders at precise angles...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: ...we'll be able to counteract the disruption and calm the turbulent kuuvahki down!

choices.text: An exquisite plan, truly!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #Right? See, this is why the Moon Ma{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}iden favors you, {NICKNAME}! You've got a sharp eye for genius!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, Paimon doesn't really get all this calculating and analyzing, but Paimon's not sure she can trust anything you say, Verna...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Well, we won't know unless we try! But there's a problem — Kraka V and Kraka VII, who went looking for stone fragments, still haven't come back...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: V and VII? Now that you say that, Paimon does remember you mentioning a Kraka... III, was it?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: That's right. Kraka V and Kraka VII are its successor models. These little fellows are amazing helpers. If only the original, Kraka I, was still around... well, that's a long story for another time.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: I wish I could go find them myself, but my nose started bleeding like crazy after I took a few steps in...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And that's where we need to step in, right?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Oh my, Paimon! You're just as warm and kind as you look! Thank you so much for volunteering to help me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's not doing this just for you! Th—This is for everyone's sake!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, why'd Paimon say something like that...? Umm, in any case, everything will be okay as long as we help find Kraka V and VII and those stone fragments, right?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Yes, and once you've collected the stone fragments, just toss them up onto those two large stones! That's the beauty of a proper scientific solution — it works no matter who tries it!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #Alright, my ever-reliable {NICKNAME} and Paimon, I'll be counting on you!

choices.text: That's... not what I'd call foolproof.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Haha, I get it. When I first looked over the results of my calculations, I thought, "Wait. Can this even be?" But numbers don't lie. You'll see!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No matter how serious you sound, it doesn't change how crazy this plan is!

choices.text: I see... Looks like we can't just walk away from this.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Ah, I knew I had a good eye— Uh... I mean, I knew trusting the Moon Ma{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}iden to bless me with saviors such as yourselves was a good idea!

choices.text: Whoa! That kuuvahki power is intense...! Paimon, run! I'll cover you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait, seriously?! {NICKNAME}, are you okay? ... Hey! Don't mess around, would ya? Nothing happened!

choices.text: The little one's Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #And the big one's {NICKNAME}... hey! What are we, some kind of comedy duo now?

choices.text: Should I be wearing that green uniform from the Adventurers' Guild instead?

talks.objective: Enter the cave and search for fragment(s)
Throw the fragment(s) at the stone

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: We found it! See? I told you to trust in the power of science...
...You arrive at last, hero of "Elysium."

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Whoa! There's someone else here too!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?
I am the dawn's first breath upon the world's weary brow, the final draught of nectar drawn from a bitter well. I am mother to all, and daughter to all...

choices.text: Is that a prayer?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Eh? Let me think... That does sound like part of a rite — but it's a verse only a Moonchanter is allowed to recite...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Hmph, a true priestess would never get the sequence of their prayers wrong. Another fraud in a borrowed robe — I've seen plenty of your kind!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Last time it was a woman called Hidimbi, she too dressed the part, played the role, and fooled quite a few...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: But tough luck for you, imposter — you've got a real priestess right here! And I can see through your disguise!
...Do the mask's carvings determine the actor's worth? What matters is that she sits in that seat, and thus she plays the role...
In this sublunary sphere, are we not all masked? It is merely that some veils can be seen, and others, not...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woah... That sounds profound. If nothing else, she sounds more priestess-y than you, Verna...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Hey! What's that supposed to mean?

choices.text: I can't help but agree...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Ugh, you outsiders are so easily tricked — ignore the sweet words and look past the surface for once, why don't you?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Ugh, never mind! According to my calculations, you've hidden the fragment we're looking for inside this Moon Mirror, isn't that right?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: That's no trinket for common hands. Hand it over, or... or I'll use the Moon Goddess's favor to give your head a very enthusiastic blessing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you a priestess or a thug, Verna!?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: What, you want me to bow, kiss the forehead of this scammer, and sing her a dainty hymn while we're at it!? Now's not the time for etiquette!
...Your desires unfurl before me like threads... And I have traced their destined weave.
But this is no place for us to speak. Walk with me, and I shall lay bare the tapestry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Where did she go? She just disappeared...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That strange lady... who exactly is she? She doesn't seem like a bad person...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Scammers never seem like villains when you first see them. That's exactly how they pull the wool over their victims' eyes!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Who knows where she stole our garb from... but she can't fool me. I knew she was a fake the instant I laid eyes on her!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't get all this religious stuff... but even though she talks funny, she sounds so gentle and kind...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: I—I can speak more gently too, you know!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: That imposter just happens to have a nicer manner of speech, greater skill in channeling the Moon Goddes{RUBY#[D]kuuvahki}s's blessing, and more experience with using the Moon Mirror...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Ugh, alright, alright! I know she looks more like a Frostmoon priestess than I do!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: But that doesn't matter now — I'm the real one and she's the fake! What matters is catching up to her and taking that fragment back!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Let's follow the Moonlane up this way. It may be an old method with zero scientific basis, but since we're out of options, we might as well!

choices.text: It's okay, Verna. Even if you're an imposter...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Excuse you! I'm not the imposter, she is!

choices.text: Seems like this place is turning into a gathering spot for priestesses...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: That does sound like part of a rite — but it's a verse only a Moonchanter is allowed to recite...

talks.objective: Enter the cave and search for fragment(s)

dialogues.text: ...We meet again, hero of "Elysium."

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Get it right — It's heroes, plural! Now hand over the fragment, imposter!

choices.text: Pretty please.

response.text: ...Is what you seek not right before your eyes?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Haha, I knew you wouldn't give up without a fight! Guess I'll just have to give you that blessing to the head — Wait, what did you just say?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: You're just... giving it to us? Then why have us come all this way in the first place?
Because this is where it must happen. Fate demands it. I have waited too long, endured too much, all for this moment. All for the birth of a "god"...
But it matters not. Soon it will end, and the newborn "god" will drape the world in true joy...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What are you even talking about?
...Via... I have glimpsed it in the mirror of stars. There is no place for her in a world where the "god" has now been born...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: First off, it's Verna, not Via! Don't you know it's rude to— Wait, you weren't talking about me, were you?
Indeed. So then — do what must be done. The ending you seek awaits.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, wait, wait. We're not here to hurt you or anything! You're just so vague and cryptic all the time — it's getting on Paimon's nerves!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And what's with the kuuvahki turbulence around here? Why is that fragment in your hands? This "ending we seek" would sure be nice with an explanation of... well, anything!
...Patience. Once all comes to an end, we will meet again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh?
You seek answers, do you not? When the moment comes, the path ahead will open.
Well then, I shall await you at the Court of the First Edict.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Huh? But isn't the Court of the First Edict already...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "O nightingale, O nightingale, who soars above pale ridges and frozen plains..."\n"Have you heard the songs of evening prayer? My dearest nightingale..."

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Hey! Stop right there!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whoa, {NICKNAME}, watch out! Looks like something's woken up!

choices.text: You heard the lady! Hand it over!

talks.objective: Enter the cave and search for fragment(s)

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Argh! This is unbelievable! Who does this fraud think she is!? The nerve of her — taking control of a sacred Frostnight Scion and turning it against us...!

choices.text: We'll be giving that head of hers a blessing AND a sermon!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Anyway, first things first — let's gather the remaining kuuhenki on the island, extract the last fragment from the Moon Mirror, and stabilize the disturbance once and for all!

choices.text: Is she really taking control of it, I wonder...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—Yeah... Paimon thinks there's a good chance that it was the lightning strikes from earlier that woke the Frostnight Scion up...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Well, then that, too, must've been her doing! If she can wield kuuvahki and knows our prayers inside and out, pulling off something like that would be a piece of cake!

talks.objective: Enter the cave and search for fragment(s)

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Anyway, first things first — let's gather the remaining kuuhenki on the island, extract the last fragment from the Moon Mirror, and stabilize the disturbance once and for all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: W—What should we do? Doesn't look like we can leave through here... Wait, Paimon sees some light over there! Maybe there's another way around?

talks.objective: Throw the fragment(s) at the stone

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: #Alright, my ever-reliable {NICKNAME} and Paimon, I'll be counting on you! Once you've collected the stone fragments, just toss them up onto those two large stones!

talks.objective: Talk to Verna

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! What's going on now? The kuuvahki feels even more unstable than before!

choices.text: Is this all part of the plan?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: No need to panic! This is just... a minor technical issue. Nothing to worry about!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: We've successfully adjusted the kuuvahki from a chaotic state to a reversed chaotic state. Now we just need to nudge it back to normal!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Think about it this way: If things have already gone from bad to incomprehensible, there's no room left for it to get any worse, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Your explanation is what's incomprehensible! How can you stay so calm when everything's falling apart?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: B—Because panicking won't help! Staying calm... l—lets us think clearly and find a way out of this mess...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #I—I'm sorry, I'm sorry! I lied! I'm totally freaking out, I'm just trying to look like I'm not! {NICKNAME}, Paimon, what in the Moon's name are we supposed to do!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you're just going to dump the problem on us now? Hey, if you're really a priestess of the Frostmoon Scions, don't you have some kinda prayer or spell that can stop the storm?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: You say it like such things exist! Ugh. That's why we place our trust in science... Yes, we've still got science, don't we? Now let me check...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Aha, just as I suspected! Kraka III's readings suggest a source of faint kuuvahki traces nearby, almost identical to that of the other fragments.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: If the first two fragments tipped the kuuvahki into a reversed chaotic state, then the third one should be able to bring it to a state of minimized turbulence... Yep, that has to be it!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #Ha! So it was just a miscalculation after all! I knew the plan itself was absolutely foolproof. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, this way!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Looks like we don't have any other leads... Might as well follow Verna. Come on, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: So much for that "intricate" plan of yours...

talks.objective: Search for new fragment(s) nearby

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Eureka! See? I told you to trust in the power of science...
...You arrive at last, hero of "Elysium."

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Whoa! There's someone else here too!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on... This one seems familiar... If Paimon's memory serves, she gave us directions last time, when we ran into that giant crab!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But now she's shown up again... Hey, who are you, really?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: See? All according to plan. The kuuvahki turbulence has been neutralized!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was NOTHING like your original plan! With all the accidents along the way, Paimon can't tell if you're optimistic or just shameless!

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: I'll take that as a compliment! After all, being pessimistic and risk-averse won't get us through situations like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... Fair enough. But Paimon can't help but wonder, why are you out here all on your own? Shouldn't the other Scions be helping out in some way?

dialogues.speaker: Verna
dialogues.text: Well... *sigh* Since you've helped me get this far, I suppose I should come clean. This island is... in a way, considered a forbidden place to us Frostmoon Scions. And I may have committed an even greater sin...

choices.text: Forbidden? But we were able to just walk in...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: In our territories, that's not so uncommon. What truly holds people back isn't the walls they see — but the ones they've built within their hearts.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since when did you get so philosophical?... Hey, wait! Don't dodge the question!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Ahem, seriously though... I wanted to try solving the problem using robots. You probably know this already, but most of us Frostmoon Scions aren't exactly big fans of tech.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: I thought if my plan went well this time, maybe I could finally convince those block-headed... Well, I mean, those very steady, if rather conservative, higher-ups to reconsider their stance.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Hold on... I can say that, can't I? Technically, the robots were part of our operation, and since we succeeded, they clearly played their part in our success, right?

choices.text: Even though the "part" they played wasn't constructive...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Hmm... Maybe I'll gloss over that part when I explain it later... *sigh* Still, that probably wouldn't work, would it...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: But hey! If not this time, then there's always next time. I'll keep pushing forward, and one day these little fellas will make a big difference. I believe they will!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, but before we talk about the future... Those two big rocks, they flew off in that direction, right?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: They did. And... Hmm. If we go that way, we'll end up at the Court of the First Edict...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Court of the First Edict... Wait, isn't that where that strange lady — y'know, the one who seemed even more priestess-y than you do, Verna — said she was headed?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: You're breaking my heart, Paimon! Even now, you still think that suspicious lady's priestess act is more convincing than I am...

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Ahem, anyway, I'm sure she was just bluffing. Because... Well, the Court of the First Edict was sealed off five hundred years ago.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: That place used to be one of our sacred sites. Five hundred years ago, Lady Aila, the Moonchanter who witnessed the birth of the Moon Ma{RUBY#[D]Kuutar}iden, personally sealed it shut.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Forget some outsider con artist — even after generations of Moonchanters, no one has ever broken the seal Lady Aila placed. It's not for a lack of trying... just that no one's ever succeeded.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, but that leaves us with no clue at all! How are we supposed to track her down now?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Don't worry, I've already come up with another brilliant plan!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Although... it might need just a tiny bit of prep. Just a little. Probably...?

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #Okay, I'll go clean up the robots first. Thanks for all the help, {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: "O fair Frost Moon, weave for me a gentle hymn, and bless the nightingale-hearted wayfarers. For ye have stolen the fell curse of the north wind, and the silver spire that sought to pierce the firmament shall no longer..."

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Shall no longer... uhh... Haha, well, I never did memorize Lady Aila's prayers properly. Anyway — thank you, and may we meet again!

choices.text: Pretty sure my part in your success was far greater!

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: #Of course! Your contribution is beyond question, {NICKNAME}. But for the greater good, sometimes a little... rhetorical embellishment is necessary. *sigh* Ugh, I can't even convince myself...

choices.text: So... you've finally dropped the act.

response.speaker: Verna
response.text: Hehehe, since I've been found out, there's no point keeping up the act any lon— W—Wait, wait! I'm just kidding! Don't draw your weapon!
